requirement: The Constitution shall remain valid regardless of changes to frontend, backend, database, or integration technologies.
The platform must fulfill governance obligations defined by this Constitution from a governance perspective.
All subordinate governance, UX, workflow, access control, and implementation documents shall conform to this Constitution.
When documents conflict, the higher-level document shall always prevail.
No subordinate document may override or contradict this Constitution.
The official governance library shall maintain the DX OSE Constitution at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain the DX OSE UX Constitution at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain Business Decision Records (BDR) at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain Workflow Contracts at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain the Access Control Catalog (ACC) at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain the Architecture Guide at minimum.
The official governance library shall maintain the Implementation Guide at minimum.
Normative keywords shall be interpreted exactly as defined in Chapter 1.4.
DX OSE shall provide one consistent document lifecycle experience across all operational modules.
Internal workflow implementation must never be exposed to end users.
Internal workflow step names must never be exposed to end users.
Internal status codes must never be exposed to end users.
Each user-facing lifecycle state shall represent one consistent business meaning across the entire DX OSE ERP Platform.
No module may redefine the standardized user-facing lifecycle state meanings.
No module may introduce additional user-facing lifecycle states unless first ratified in this Constitution.
A separate user-facing state named Cancelled shall not be introduced unless ratified in this Constitution.
Each module shall provide a consistent mapping between internal workflow states and standardized user-facing lifecycle states.
Internal workflow identifiers must never be exposed to end users.
Internal status codes must never be exposed to end users.
Internal enum names must never be exposed to end users.
Internal workflow step names must never be exposed to end users.
Other internal implementation details must never be exposed to end users.
Identical business outcomes shall always resolve to the same standardized user-facing lifecycle state across the DX OSE platform.
Posting is the single business commit point for all operational and financial effects within the DX OSE ERP Platform.
No operational or financial effect shall be considered official before Posting unless this Constitution explicitly states otherwise.
Operational reports shall derive operational and financial results exclusively from Posted documents.
Editability shall be governed exclusively by document lifecycle state, not by individual screen implementations.
Documents in Draft state shall be editable.
Documents in Returned state shall be editable.
Documents in Submitted state shall not be editable.
Documents in In Review state shall not be editable.
Documents in Posted state shall not be editable.
Documents in Rejected state shall not be editable.
Documents in Void or Cancelled state shall not be editable.
Documents in Closed state shall not be editable.
Delete is permitted only while the document is in Draft.
Once a document leaves Draft, Delete must not be available.
Business termination shall use governed lifecycle actions (Cancel, Reject, Void, Close, etc.) instead of Delete after Draft.
Once a document enters the governed lifecycle, business termination actions shall replace deletion.
After Return, the workflow path shall be Edit then Submit.
There shall be no separate action named Re-submit.
Submit shall always represent entering the workflow, whether for the first time or after Return.
After Reject, the same document must not re-enter workflow.
After Reject, a new document is required to repeat the operation.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing current state when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing workflow step when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing actor when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing date and time when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing mandatory reasons when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing workflow comments when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing system events when applicable.
Every document detail view shall present a unified timeline showing duration when applicable.
Users shall see only the actions they need for their role and document state.
Action behavior shall remain consistent across all DX OSE modules regardless of workflow implementation.
No module may invent alternative names for standard actions unless ratified in this Constitution.
Cancel is an action, not a lifecycle state.
Alternative Cancel labels with the same meaning (Abort, Discard, Cancel Document) must not be used.
Reviewer actions shall be available only while the document is actively assigned to the current reviewer according to workflow definition and the permission model.
Send Back shall not end the document.
Send Back shall allow edit.
Send Back shall require a reason.
Send Back next step shall be Edit then Submit.
Send Back shall continue the business transaction.
Reject shall end the document.
Reject shall not allow edit.
Reject shall require a reason.
Reject next step shall require a new document if the operation repeats.
Reject shall terminate the business transaction.
There shall be only one primary action for the current document state.
Button order shall be Primary, then Secondary, then Neutral, then Danger.
Operation permissions govern authorization only.
Operation permissions shall never replace workflow validation.
Operation permissions shall never replace lifecycle validation.
Operation permissions shall never replace business rule enforcement.
The Access Control Catalog (ACC) is the single source of truth for permissions.
Evidence Package does not require a separate permission in the current DX OSE release.
Permissions shall never bypass document lifecycle rules.
Permissions grant eligibility, not execution authority.
Action Allowed shall equal Permission plus Workflow plus Lifecycle plus Business Rules plus Scope.
Modules shall not introduce alternative operation names for standardized operations.
Posting is the single irreversible business commit point for all operational and financial effects within the DX OSE Platform.
Posting is the only operation permitted to create official operational and financial business effects.
Documents become business-immutable after Posting except through formally governed reversal or adjustment procedures.
Before Posting, the platform shall verify user authority.
Before Posting, the platform shall verify valid workflow state.
Before Posting, the platform shall verify open inventory/financial period for Posting Date.
Before Posting, the platform shall perform full document revalidation.
Before Posting, the platform shall verify stock availability for outbound documents.
Full revalidation shall occur immediately before Posting regardless of prior validation.
Posting shall use a single transactional boundary.
Partial posting is prohibited.
Any posting failure shall leave the document and related business data completely unchanged.
Repeating the same posting request shall never create additional effects.
Posting shall be automatically triggered upon successful final workflow approval unless a document-specific governance policy defines otherwise.
Final Workflow Approval equals business authorization for Posting.
No additional posting confirmation is required by default.
Posting behavior shall remain deterministic and repeat-safe throughout the platform.
Each document shall permanently maintain Document Date.
Each document shall permanently maintain Posting Date.
Each document shall permanently maintain Assigned Posting Period.
Document Date and Posting Date must never be treated as interchangeable.
Posting is permitted only when Posting Period is Open and all validations pass.
Future posting restrictions shall apply to Posting Date only, not Document Date.
Posting into a Closed period is prohibited.
Periods shall close sequentially.
Periods must not overlap.
Period validation shall be centralized.
Modules shall not implement independent period logic.
Assigned Posting Period shall be immutable after Posting.
Period Close validation phase shall use centralized validation with progress indication when Close Period is initiated.
The platform shall provide governed period-close resolution whenever blocking conditions exist, rather than merely rejecting the request.
Document State Protection and Draft and Recovery must remain separate policies.
Every operational document shall begin as a server-recognized draft unless Workflow Contracts define otherwise.
The platform shall define draft owner.
The platform shall define draft access rights.
The platform shall define draft ownership transfer rules if permitted.
The platform shall define handling of drafts for inactive or departed users.
Rules for opening the same draft from multiple sessions or devices shall align with Chapter 8 (Concurrency).
Auto-save shall occur on meaningful business events.
Auto-save shall occur on add or delete row.
Auto-save shall occur on quantity or price change.
Auto-save shall occur on supplier or warehouse change.
Auto-save shall occur on attachment change.
Auto-save shall occur on notes change.
Auto-save shall occur before navigation.
Recovered drafts shall not bypass current validation.
Restored documents must be revalidated before continue or submit.
A draft registry is required per document family.
Default draft retention shall be 30 days.
Draft expiration policy (delete, archive, expired state) shall be defined by platform policy.
Document State Protection shall apply to route navigation.
Document State Protection shall apply to browser refresh.
Document State Protection shall apply to browser or tab close.
Document State Protection shall apply to back navigation.
Document State Protection shall apply to session expiration with unsaved changes.
Successful Save Draft or Submit shall return the document to a clean state.
Upon successful creation of the first Server Draft, the System Document Number becomes permanently reserved per Chapter 9.
Every editable document shall maintain a Concurrency Version for conflict detection.
Concurrency shall apply to the entire governed document, not isolated fields only.
Concurrent edits must be detected at the Draft stage.
Last write wins is prohibited for concurrent draft edits.
Conflicting draft operations shall be rejected.
Users shall reload the latest version after a conflicting draft operation.
After Submit, the document shall be read-only except via Return workflow.
Save Draft must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Submit must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Approve must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Reject must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Send Back must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Cancel must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Post must not execute twice on the same version without detection.
Posting must not execute except on the latest valid document version after concurrency verification.
The platform shall reject conflicting updates.
The platform shall not overwrite another user's changes during conflict.
The platform shall require reload before retry after a conflicting update.
Concurrency conflicts shall be recorded in audit when appropriate.
System Document Numbers shall be assigned by the platform only.
Users must not enter System Document Numbers.
Users must not edit System Document Numbers.
System Document Numbers shall be assigned at first Server Draft Save.
System Document Number format shall be {Type Prefix}-{Year}-{Sequence}.
External references such as supplier invoice numbers shall be separate fields from System Document Numbers.
System Document Numbers shall be unique within governed numbering scope.
Upon first Server Draft, the System Document Number shall be permanently reserved.
Numbers from deleted drafts shall never be released or recycled.
Number gaps are acceptable but numbers must not be reused.
All creation channels (manual, import, integration, future) shall use the same numbering governance.
Document number prefixes shall be governed centrally.
Modules must not configure document number prefixes independently unless authorized.
Gaps from failed or rolled-back number allocation operations are acceptable.
Once assigned, a System Document Number shall be immutable for the entire document lifecycle.
System Document Number allocation shall be traceable through platform audit mechanisms.
Manual override of System Document Numbers is prohibited.
System Document Number sequences shall reset annually per prefix per year or fiscal year per platform policy.
Inbound movement documents shall not require stock check at posting.
Outbound movement documents shall require stock check at posting.
Stock availability shall be validated against the latest committed inventory state at Posting.
Negative inventory is prohibited in DX OSE v2.0.
Quantity must be greater than zero.
Zero-quantity lines are prohibited.
Quantity precision shall follow platform settings and validation shall use precise values.
Stock validation shall be against the source inventory location defined by the transaction.
All inventory calculations shall use the base unit.
No transaction shall violate constitutional stock integrity rules.
Inventory movements shall be generated exclusively by Posted transactions.
Posted inventory movements shall never be edited.
Posted inventory movement corrections shall be made via new governed transactions.
Inbound documents shall not require stock check at posting.
Outbound stock validation shall be authoritative on the platform.
Client-side outbound stock checks may warn only and shall not be authoritative.
Valuation at Posting shall follow Chapter 5 posting rules.
Any stock balance with qtyOnHand greater than zero must have wacUnitCost greater than zero.
qtyOnHand equal to zero with wacUnitCost equal to zero is always allowed.
Any posting that would produce qtyOnHand greater than zero with wacUnitCost less than or equal to zero must be rejected at the write point.
There is no free-of-charge (FOC) or zero-price inbound path; inbound quantity greater than zero requires a strictly positive unit price or unit cost.

WAC integrity SHALL be enforced via shared guards assertNoZeroWacWithQty and assertPositiveUnitCostForInboundQty on GRN, Movement, Inventory Count, Get Pass, Transfer, and Legacy count/report posting doors.
All operational inventory quantities SHALL be whole numbers (integers). Fractional quantities are prohibited.
Fractional quantity entry or posting on GRN, Transfer, Inventory Count, Movement, Get Pass, Breakage, and Lost MUST be rejected with a clear operator message.
Integer quantity integrity SHALL be enforced via shared guard assertIntegerQuantity (or equivalent) at input and posting write points.

ItemUnit.conversionRate on Item Master SHALL be a positive integer; fractional conversion rates MUST be rejected on item unit save. Document posting paths may still use identity qty (no conversion multiply) until explicitly enabled.
Changing display currency shall change symbol and format only.
Display currency must not convert amounts.
Display currency must not alter stored values.
Display currency must not alter ledger data.
Display currency must not alter valuation.
Display currency must not alter historical posted documents.
Display currency must not participate in financial calculations.
Display currency must not participate in inventory valuation.
Display currency must not participate in posting logic.
Display currency must not participate in taxation.
Display currency must not participate in accounting transactions.
Display Currency shall apply consistently across all user interfaces unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Display Currency shall apply consistently across reports unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Display Currency shall apply consistently across dashboards unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Display Currency shall apply consistently across exported documents unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Display Currency shall apply consistently across printed outputs unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Reports and PDF shall use property display currency as each channel is brought under this standard.
Changing Property Display Currency must not modify historical posted documents.
Changing Property Display Currency must not modify stored business data.
Optional header fields omitted when not applicable shall not cause positions to shift arbitrarily.
System header fields including document number, status, created by/at, and posted by/at must not be user-editable.
Header fields shall become read-only once the document enters a non-editable lifecycle state unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Changes to property, department, or warehouse after lines exist or after workflow progress must require confirmation.
Changes to property, department, or warehouse after lines exist or after workflow progress shall follow document business rules.
Header information and document lines shall remain logically consistent throughout the lifecycle unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Modules adding header fields shall preserve standard header order and positions.
Each document line shall maintain a unique internal identity independent of display order or row number.
Posted document lines shall be immutable.
Posted document line corrections shall be made via new governed business transactions.
Line values and calculated fields shall recalculate automatically per governed business rules when relevant data changes.
All document lines shall remain consistent with governing business context in the header unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Document totals must not be directly user-editable.
Line totals must not be directly user-editable.
Duplicate line behavior shall be defined by each business document according to functional requirements.
Significant line-level business changes shall be auditable per platform audit policy.
Large document line datasets shall not degrade usability per Chapter 27.
Posted attachments shall not be modified except by explicit admin governance.
Posted attachments shall not be replaced except by explicit admin governance.
Posted attachments shall not be deleted except by explicit admin governance.
Required attachments must block submit when missing.
The platform shall enforce allowed attachment file types per platform policy.
The platform shall enforce maximum attachment file size per platform policy.
The platform shall enforce maximum attachment count per platform policy.
Uploaded attachment files shall comply with platform security validation policy.
Attachment download shall be subject to the same authorization as document view.
Attachment filenames must not serve as internal identifiers.
All attachment operations shall be auditable.
Reject shall require a reason where defined.
Send Back shall require a reason where defined.
Cancel shall require a reason where defined.
Workflow comments shall become immutable once recorded.
System notes shall become immutable once recorded.
Audit comments shall become immutable once recorded.
System notes shall be generated exclusively by the platform.
Users must not manually create system notes.
Users must not manually modify system notes.
Notes and comments shall appear in chronological order within the unified timeline.
Item images are Item Master data.
Item images must not be created through transactional documents.
Item images must not be modified through transactional documents.
Item images shall have a single source in Item Master.
A standardized placeholder shall be shown when no item image exists.
Item images in grids shall use thumbnails, not full resolution.
Maximum item image size shall be 1 MB per image.
Supported item image formats and dimensions shall follow platform media policy.
Unified export behavior shall apply when an item image is absent.
Keyboard navigation shall be keyboard-first across governed experiences.
Enter shall move to the next field and shall not submit, post, or delete.
Enter at row end shall move to the next row or add a row.
Shift+Enter shall move to the previous field.
Enter in a textarea shall insert a new line.
Esc shall close lookup, calendar, or small overlay components.
Tab shall follow standard browser focus order.
Invalid fields shall retain focus.
After item pick in line entry, focus shall move to quantity.
Keyboard behavior shall be consistent across all modules.
Focus shall be visually distinguishable.
Keyboard navigation shall skip disabled controls.
Keyboard navigation shall skip hidden controls.
Dialogs shall assign initial focus to the primary interactive element.
Global shortcuts shall be centrally governed.
Modules must not introduce independent global shortcuts.
Each error type shall use exactly one display channel.
Validation errors shall disappear when fixed.
On submit, focus shall move to the first validation error.
When many errors exist, the summary banner shall show the error count.
When many errors exist, error details shall appear at fields or rows.
All validation and error messages shall support localization.
Backend validation shall return codes.
The platform shall present translated text for backend validation codes.
Validation shall be deterministic: same input and conditions shall produce the same result.
Validation shall occur at data entry per business rules.
Validation shall occur at workflow actions per business rules.
Validation shall occur at posting per business rules.
Client-side validation shall assist only.
Server-side validation shall be authoritative.
Validation messages shall be presented in logical order: header, then lines, then document.
Warnings shall be informational unless governed otherwise.
Validation errors shall block the operation.
The same error must not be duplicated across display channels.
Error placement shall match severity.
Errors must not use duplicate display channels.
User-facing error messages shall be clear and actionable.
User-facing error messages shall be free of technical implementation details.
Stack traces must never be exposed to end users.
SQL details must never be exposed to end users.
Internal IDs must never be exposed to end users in error messages.
Equivalent error conditions shall produce consistent error codes and user experience.
The first validation error shall be focusable.
The first validation error shall be announced to assistive technology.
Notifications shall use a unified dictionary.
Notifications for the same event shall be deduplicated.
Notifications must not rely on color alone.
The platform must not notify a user to open a document they cannot access.
Loading scope shall match the operation scope.
Long operations shall show progress or status.
Action buttons shall be disabled during the action.
Double submission is prohibited.
Partial operations must not block the entire application.
If loading exceeds a reasonable duration, the user shall be informed the operation continues.
Every workflow action must generate an audit record.
Every significant attachment change must generate an audit record.
Every significant line change must generate an audit record.

The document timeline shall be a single chronological Workflow Timeline. Order contract (platform SSOT; Get Pass is the reference implementation): HISTORY by actedAt as Submit → Approvals → Send Back → Resubmit → Approvals…; then CURRENT; then FUTURE pending steps by stepNumber. Module builders emit audits/entries; assignGlobalOrder is the only ordering authority.
Audit records shall be immutable.
Audit timestamps shall be stored internally in UTC.
Audit timestamps shall be displayed per user time zone.
Timeline filtering is permitted without altering audit records.
Lookup behavior shall be unified for items, parties, locations, and references.
Lookup profiles (Receiving, stock-based, catalog, issue) shall use the same UX with differing data scope only.
Lookup search shall support code, name, and barcode.
Lookup search ranking shall be exact code, then exact barcode, then prefix, then contains.
Lookup search shall debounce before executing search.
Lookup search shall normalize case and spaces insensitively.
Lookup keyboard navigation shall support arrow up and arrow down.
Lookup keyboard navigation shall support Enter, Esc, and Tab.
Lookup shall close on select.
Lookup shall close on outside click.
Lookup shall close on field exit.
Only one lookup shall be open at a time.
After item pick in line entry, focus shall move to quantity.
Lookup loading, no-results, and error-with-retry states shall use unified messaging.
Lookup shall use unified empty states.
Lookup results shall be filtered by permission to show only authorized data.
Lookup shall enforce tenant isolation with no cross-tenant data.
Large lookup result sets shall use paging or infinite scroll per platform policy.
Large catalogs shall use server-side search.
Loading entire large catalogs into the client is prohibited.
Operational data entry shall be desktop only for v2.0.
Minimum supported resolution shall be 1366x768.
Zoom support from 80% to 125% is required for release acceptance.
Pages shall not require horizontal page scroll except inside grids.
Titles shall not be clipped.
Buttons shall not overlap.
Create screen primary actions shall be visible at 1366x768 and 100% zoom.
Dialogs shall fit the viewport with internal scroll.
Tables shall scroll internally.
Supported browsers shall follow the platform browser support matrix.
High DPI displays (2K/4K) shall be supported.
Multi-monitor presentation shall be consistent.
Responsive test matrix 1366x768 at 80/90/100/110/125% zoom is required for Definition of Done.
Responsive test matrix 1440/1600/1920 at 100% zoom is required for Definition of Done.
Modules must not invent unrelated document layouts.
All modules must declare and follow one document layout archetype.
Primary scroll owner shall be defined per document layout archetype.
Primary scroll owner shall be consistent per archetype.
Print and PDF export must match.
Printed and exported documents shall include status watermarks such as draft, posted, and void.
Printed and exported documents shall include header and footer with organization identity.
Printed and exported documents shall include page numbers and print metadata.
The platform electronic record is authoritative over printed or exported copies.
Print shall be subject to the same permission model as document view.
Export shall be subject to the same permission model as document view.
Export authorization shall be explicit.
Sensitive data shall be masked per authorization on export and print.
Large lists shall use paging or virtual presentation.
Server-assisted search shall be used when warranted for large lists.
Search requests shall use debounce and cancel in-flight requests.
Heavy export and print operations shall be asynchronous with user feedback.
Interactive elements shall be labeled.
Color shall not be the sole state indicator.
Contrast shall meet agreed accessibility targets.
The platform shall support screen reader compatibility for governed interactions.
Validation messages shall be accessible to assistive technology.
Error messages shall be accessible to assistive technology.
New capabilities must declare applicable Constitution chapters before release.
Revised capabilities must declare applicable Constitution chapters before release.
New and revised capabilities must demonstrate Constitution compliance before release.
A screen or capability is compliant only when all mandatory rules in applicable chapters are satisfied.
Compliance Definition of Done shall include the responsive test matrix where applicable.
Exceptions require documented approval, scope, expiry, and registration.
Exceptions must not weaken audit rules.
Exceptions must not weaken posting rules.
Exceptions must not weaken period rules.
New operational modules must undergo constitutional review before production approval.
QA shall validate against this Constitution and the UX Constitution.
A conformance backlog shall not override the Constitution.
The platform shall provide a unified client DraftManager with save, restore, list, delete, and clear operations.
Draft storage keys shall include tenantId, userId, screenKey, optional entityId, and mandatory schemaVersion.
When schemaVersion is compatible, the platform shall restore the draft.
When schemaVersion is upgradeable and a migration is registered, the platform shall migrate then restore.
When schemaVersion is incompatible, the platform shall ignore the draft and notify the user.
DraftManager save, delete, and clear operations shall be idempotent where possible.
DraftManager restore shall not mutate stored draft or server draft state.
DraftManager clear with draftId shall remove the local draft and the linked server draft when entityId is bound.
Local draft persistence shall use configurable debounce and periodic snapshot intervals per approved platform configuration.
Local drafts shall not replace server-recognized drafts required by Chapter 7.2.
DraftManager shall emit observable draft continuity events per the platform telemetry contract without including secrets or full draft payloads.
After GRN pilot sign-off, draft continuity shall generalize to Transfer, Stock Count, Adjustment, and Purchase Order per BDR-010.
scope: GRN, Transfer, Stock Count, Adjustment, Purchase Order

requirement: Draft-stage file selection shall upload to temporary storage and store attachmentId in the draft payload.
Draft payloads shall not embed binary attachment content.
Unlinked temporary attachments shall be deleted automatically per a configurable retention policy defined in approved platform configuration.
Temporary attachment upload, link, replace, cleanup, and download shall be auditable.
Session continuity shall be a platform-wide policy; modules shall not implement independent token refresh or session-timeout logic.
AuthService shall be limited to login, logout, token storage, and refresh execution.
SessionManager shall handle proactive refresh scheduling, idle detection, and session-end recovery coordination.
HTTP Interceptor shall perform single-flight token refresh and one request retry on TOKEN_EXPIRED only as a fallback mechanism.
Proactive refresh shall be scheduled before access-token expiry using a configurable safety margin per approved platform configuration.
Proactive refresh shall execute only while the session is Active.
Idle detection shall apply a configurable idle policy using approved activity signals and idle duration from platform configuration.
Proactive refresh shall be suspended while the session is Idle.
On resume from Idle, a valid refresh token shall renew the access token; otherwise the session shall end.
Session end shall flush drafts, display a clear message, persist returnUrl, restore after login, and skip leave-page guard for expiry redirect.
REQ-SESSION-RECOVERY-001: After successful re-login caused by session expiry, the platform shall restore returnUrl and available draft data without requiring the user to re-enter persisted fields.
SessionManager shall emit observable session continuity events per the platform telemetry contract.
Continuity telemetry events shall not include access tokens, refresh tokens, passwords, or full draft payloads.
Session continuity logic shall not terminate the session during an in-flight tenant switch request.
The repository root shall contain only the OSE-backend and OSE-Frontend application projects.
The repository root shall not contain temporary folders, runtime logs, editor configuration, generated files, or miscellaneous directories without an approved Governance structural exception.
Platform Constitution and governance SSOT shall reside under OSE-backend/docs/governance/.
Any future structural change to the repository root shall be documented through Governance before implementation.
